messages:
Alex M.: Heads up — trying to bring up OpenGen-7B (community checkpoint) for evals and quant experiments. Need a quick license/compliance check before we run quant and potentially redistribute converted weights to infra. @Jen R. @Maya P. :eyes:
Maya P.: Looks like main repo points to a model card and license link: https://huggingface.co/opengen/OpenGen-7B/blob/main/MODEL_CARD.md — license header says CC-BY-NC-4.0.
Sam K.: cc: if it truly is CC-BY-NC-4.0 then hosting behind our hosted API or selling is a no-go. Even sharing quantized weights externally would be problematic. Internal evals maybe fine? :thinking_face:
Jen R.: Confirming — CC-BY-NC-4.0 = non-commercial. Attribution required. Key Qs: was training data bundled with restrictions? any third-party code with more restrictive terms? we need the exact license file and model card.
Alex M.: Pasted model card excerpt:
```
license: "CC-BY-NC-4.0"
training_data_attribution: "See dataset_licenses.md"
weights_distribution: "checkpoint.tar.gz (hosted)"
```
Alex M.: Also found dataset_licenses.md referencing several datasets, some with non-commercial or research-only clauses.
LegalBot: Automated scan result: Detected license: CC-BY-NC-4.0. Flags: [non-commercial], [attribution required]. Recommendation: do not redistribute or serve commercially. Escalate to legal for dataset provenance review.
Maya P.: For our quant experiments we usually convert weights and store in S3. Can we keep everything strictly in Private (VPC) infra and mark it restricted? Would that avoid redistribution concerns?
Jen R.: Internal-only use for experimentation typically falls under "non-commercial" scope if there is no commercial exploitation. But there are gray areas: if results feed production features later, that could be a breach. Also attribution clauses require we maintain notices. Need to review dataset licenses — some may be research-only which is stricter.
Sam K.: From engineering side: two immediate asks if we proceed with evals: 1) isolate storage (dedicated S3 prefix + encryption + no public snapshots), 2) ensure any derived weights are NOT published or bundled in customer-facing images.
Infra Bot: Noted. If you create a restricted bucket, tag as "license:restricted" and apply bucket policy to deny public ACLs and cross-account replication. Enable default KMS and object-level logging.
Alex M.: Proposal: run a contained eval in Private deployment, no model-serving, log results, and open a GH ticket for legal review before any further use. Will attach model card & dataset_licenses.md. CC @Jen R.
Jen R.: Sounds good. Please include: direct license file, dataset license excerpts, list of training data sources, link to original checkpoint, and a short note about intended use (internal eval only). I'll triage within 48h.
Alex M.: Creating ticket now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/issues/412 (placeholder)
Sam K.: Quick technical Q — if we quantize (int8) but keep the same model architecture, is that considered a derivative under typical CC terms?
Jen R.: Derivative vs transformation language varies. Many CC licenses treat adaptations/transformations as derivatives. Quantized weights likely count as a derivative. So redistribution of quantized weights is risky under CC-BY-NC.
Maya P.: Alternative: shortlist Apache-2.0 models for the same evals (OpenCore-7B, LightGen-7B). If we can match quality, prefer those to avoid legal friction.
Alex M.: Agreed. I'll run a quick benchmark compare (OpenGen-7B vs OpenCore-7B) in Private and share initial numbers in the GH ticket.
Jen R.: Thanks. If anyone finds any CLA or contributor statements in the repo, flag them — they can change obligations.
Maya P.: Will also run license scanner (fossa/spdx) on the repo and paste results in the ticket.
Infra Bot: Reminder: label any artifacts from this thread with "license_review_pending" in Artifact Registry and do not promote to shared buckets until legal clears.
Alex M.: Awesome — thanks all. I'll wait for Jen's review before doing any broader experiments or moving weights around. :thumbsup:
Jen R.: Acknowledged.
Sam K.: Thanks — will hold on quant jobs until we get the greenlight. :lock:
